etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin agenda (“things that ought to be done”), future passive participle (gerundive) of agō (“I do, act, make”).

definitions.definition: A temporally organized plan for matters to be attended to.

quote.citation: 2012 July 18, Scott Tobias, “The Dark Knight Rises”, in AV Club‎[1], retrieved 2024-11-24:
quote.text: Where the Joker preys on our fears of random, irrational acts of terror, Bane has an all-consuming, dictatorial agenda that’s more stable and permanent, a New World Order that’s been planned out with the precision of a military coup.

definitions.definition: A list of matters to be taken up (as at a meeting).
A notebook used to organize and maintain such plans or lists, an agenda book, an agenda planner.

quote.citation: 2005, Linda Wilmshurst, Alan W. Brue, A Parent's Guide To Special Education: Insider Advice On How To Navigate The System And Help Your Child Succeed, →ISBN, page 145:
quote.text: A homework agenda, sometimes called a student planner, is a notebook often used to help your child keep track of daily homework assignments.

quote.citation: 2011, Spencer Marc Aronfeld, Make It Your Own Law Firm: The Ultimate Law Student's Guide to Owning, Managing, and Marketing Your Own Successful Law Firm, AuthorHouse, page 12:
quote.text: It may be better to simply buy an agenda at the drug store for five dollars, but you need to keep this stuff accurate.

quote.citation: 2011, David Campos, Rocio Delgado, Mary Esther Huerta, Reaching Out to Latino Families of English Language Learners, →ISBN, page 160:
quote.text: The children will use an agenda book that the school provides to organize their homework information. Before leaving for home, the children will neatly write their assignments and related directions in their agendas.

definitions.definition: An ulterior motive; a program of various such motives.
